description:
Two satellite maps illustrate changes in Natura 2000 (N2K) site boundaries between 2012 and 2018, demonstrating how site enlargements can exceed older Area of Interest (AoI) definitions. The underlying satellite imagery shows a landscape of forests (dark green), agricultural fields (light green/brown), and water bodies (blue).

In both maps:
*   Red outlines represent the Natura 2000 site boundaries as recorded in the 2018 Natura 2000 database.
*   Yellow outlines represent the Area of Interest (AoI) buffer, which follows the shape of the Natura 2000 site in 2012.

The left map displays a long, winding riverine Natura 2000 site, along with several smaller, isolated N2K sites. The 2018 N2K boundary (red) is generally wider than and extends beyond the 2012 AoI buffer (yellow) in numerous sections, particularly in the central and southern parts of the main linear site. The smaller N2K sites are bounded in red but lack corresponding yellow 2012 AoI buffers.

The right map focuses on a Natura 2000 site centered around a large lake, with an urban area visible to the north. The 2018 N2K site boundary (red) shows a significant enlargement compared to the 2012 AoI buffer (yellow). The red outline encompasses a much larger area of the lake and surrounding land to the south and west, clearly exceeding the extent of the yellow 2012 AoI.

The maps highlight that the 2018 Natura 2000 sites are no longer entirely covered by the 2012 N2K Area of Interest, indicating site enlargement over time.
